A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DEIM and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material. Corresponding content can be reliably matched across table renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original COCO and CrowdHuman detection experiments, component and augmentation ablations, and qualitative comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds timing, pretrained-model fine-tuning, object-density sensitivity, and training-versus-validation results.

M1.justification: Dense O2O, mosaic/mixup augmentation, MAL, and the training schedules are retained. The new caching and within-batch mixup description supplies implementation detail without establishing a change to the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: COCO and CrowdHuman detection coverage remains unchanged. The new Objects365-related experiment uses existing D-FINE pretrained weights for COCO fine-tuning; it does not report direct training or evaluation on Objects365 data.

E2.justification: Table 2 removes DAB-Deformable-DETR++ and DN-Deformable-DETR++, retaining their ordinary variants. The lightweight comparison adds a D-FINE-Nano baseline alongside its DEIM counterpart. The principal comparator families remain.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce single-4090 GPU-hour comparisons, pretrained D-FINE-X fine-tuning for 32 baseline versus 24 DEIM epochs, a 148-epoch Nano configuration, and additional density and training-set evaluations. Existing benchmark splits, resolution, and documented core hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds an excessive-density setting of approximately 50 objects per image, a training-versus-validation analysis, and a check under pretrained initialization. Table 12 reuses the existing no/default Dense O2O results as controls. Earlier component, augmentation, MAL, and qualitative analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added experiments continue reporting point estimates without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Retained results keep their values. New entries include per-epoch times of 1.181 versus 1.183 GPU hours, pretrained fine-tuning AP of 59.3 versus 59.5 at 32 versus 24 epochs, Nano AP of 42.8 versus 43.0, and density/training-AP results. Two ++ baseline result rows are removed. These are added or removed comparisons, not revised scores for retained experiments.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4, their definitions, and the mathematical treatment of matching and losses are unchanged. Neither version adds formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about Dense O2O and MAL, faster convergence, and improved real-time detection. Headline results of 54.7 and 56.5 AP are unchanged; the added experiments support existing contributions.

C2.justification: v2 interprets lower training AP with higher validation AP as reduced overfitting. It proposes positive/negative imbalance and distribution shift as possible explanations for the decline from approximately 25 to 50 objects per image, and discusses effectiveness after larger-dataset pretraining. Existing small-object limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents mosaic caching, within-batch mixup, pretrained-weight provenance, and GPU-hour measurements. It replaces the GitHub code/model pointer with a project-site pointer and removes the direct CrowdHuman configuration link. The existing hyperparameter tables retain their contents.

R1.justification: The same 46 cited works and substantive positioning against previous matching strategies, losses, and DETR architectures remain. Reference backlink changes reflect pagination rather than changes in cited research.

P1.justification: Edits include correcting 'Hungarian loss' to 'Hungarian algorithm,' clarifying the model named in a YOLO comparison, revising acknowledgements, and restarting supplementary section numbering. Short analytical passages are added, while the main narrative and section organization remain stable.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 7, 8, 12, and 13; v1 Tables 7–9 become v2 Tables 9–11. Comparator rows change, several tables move, and Figure 7 relocates to the final supplementary page with the same images. All seven figures retain their content within the same two-column design.

improvement.justification: The direct timing comparison strengthens evidence that Dense O2O adds little per-epoch overhead. Pretrained fine-tuning and density/training-validation checks provide useful additional evidence about applicability and behavior. These are modest gains because the central method and retained results remain unchanged, and small new differences lack uncertainty estimates. Removing two baseline variants and the direct configuration link slightly reduces completeness, but the added evidence provides a limited net improvement.
